transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-10-02
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Evan (Rivermark Head of Platform), Priya (ML Ops), Markus (Security), Sofia (PM)
Links shared: onboarding_deck.pdf (link), network_guide.md (link), security_packet.zip (link), runbook-draft-google.docx (link)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, uh this is Aisha from Redwood, I'll run the high level and Lina will own the runbook handoff, Diego will cover the technical benchmarks. Quick agenda: access, networking, pilot scope, security questions, and next steps.
01:12 Priya: Hi thanks, yes from Rivermark we want to get this into staging quickly — we have a two week runway before exec review. Main blockers are VPC peering setup and KMS (we need HSM later).
02:05 Diego: Got it. For peering we usually provide a terraform sample and a minimal SG list, it typically takes 1-2 days with the customer's infra team. We'll also need sample traffic profile for batch vs low-latency queries.
03:40 Evan: Quick intro — our infra runs EKS and we have a gated egress policy so any outbound to hosted providers goes through a proxy; we want Private mode but evaluating Dedicated first for throughput predictability.
04:55 Markus: From security side, SOC2 is table stakes, but we also need proof of key rotation policy and audit logs. Do you provide audit log retention and syslog forwarding?
05:30 Aisha: Yes, Redwood provides audit logs and can stream to customer S3 or syslog. We'll attach the security packet with config options, retention levels. Lina will walk through the runbook items.
07:05 Lina: Ok runbook overview — stage access, credentials, onboarding checklist, escalation path, rollback plan. We'll hand over a draft today, you can comment inline.
08:40 Sofia: Small Q — do you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning?
09:10 Diego: Yes SAML and SCIM are supported. SCIM for user provisioning is in our enterprise plan; we'll include the SAML metadata and a sample IdP configuration in the packet.
11:00 Priya: On the pilot: we plan to run 100k tokens/day across two workloads — doc summarization and a reranking job. Latency target is p95 < 400ms for interactive summarization and throughput 50 req/s for rerank. Is that realistic?
12:25 Diego: For hosted variants p95 400ms depends heavily on model choice and batching. For Dedicated with right GPU type we can hit that for quantized models. We'll propose a config in the benchmark plan.
14:20 Evan: Network question — will Redwood initiate peering or we need to open tickets with our cloud provider?
15:00 Aisha: We typically provide the peer config and your cloud infra team initiates. For Private on-prem installs, we do a direct link process — we'll provide the checklist.
16:45 Markus: KMS integration — our policy requires customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. How does Redwood hookup to external KMS/HSM?
17:30 Diego: We integrate with AWS KMS and customer-managed CMKs; for on-prem HSM we have a connector but it's a longer path. We'll capture the exact flows in the security packet.
19:05 Priya: Can we run an initial smoke benchmark in staging with limited tokens to validate end-to-end before committing to Dedicated?
19:45 Diego: Absolutely. We'll run small-scale smoke tests — two models, synthetic traffic that mirrors your token distribution. Need sample prompts and token histogram.
21:00 Sofia: About costs — how do we estimate unit costs per token for the pilot vs production?
21:35 Aisha: We'll provide an early estimate grid. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/quantization levers to reduce unit costs. The CSM will run a cost walkthrough once we have sample traffic.
23:10 Evan: Rollout plan — we want canary first in staging, then gradual ramp to production. Can Redwood support A/B routing between models and automatic fallback?
23:50 Diego: Yes, the platform supports routing policies and automatic fallbacks to smaller models if capacity is constrained; we'll show the routing config in the runbook.
25:35 Markus: Audit logs — how granular are the logs? Do they capture token-level metadata or just request metadata?
26:05 Lina: Current default includes request metadata, model version, timestamps, and request id. We can enable more detail on request bodies for customers under NDA. We'll note that as an option.
27:40 Priya: SLA questions — what's the latency SLO for Dedicated vs Hosted?
28:15 Aisha: We publish performance profiles per model; Dedicated has SLA-backed latency targets for reserved pools; we'll share the SLA doc. For Hosted there's no strict SLA but we provide latency tiers and best-effort fallbacks.
30:00 Diego: Technical deep-dive we should coordinate — we'll need to collect sequence length distributions and KV cache behavior to choose kernel configs.
31:20 Evan: Who on your side leads the benchmark run?
31:45 Diego: I'll own the benchmark plan and execution with Lina for ops; Aisha will coordinate scheduling.
33:00 Sofia: Any prework we should do before the benchmark week?
33:25 Priya: We'll extract sample prompts, token histograms, example payloads, and grant a service account with minimal permissions to a staging bucket. Expect to finish that by 10/08.
35:10 Aisha: Ok timeline — today 10/02 runbook draft and security packet, by 10/04 Aisha sends onboarding docs, by 10/08 customer shares payloads, by 10/10 Diego provides benchmark plan, and week of 10/20 we run smoke/benchmarks. Does that work?
36:30 Markus: Yes, but I'll need our compliance lead looped in. Can you include contact details in the security packet?
37:10 Lina: We'll include the contact template and owner escalations in the runbook.
38:55 Priya: Are there any limitations with model versions or quantized weights we should be aware of for reranking accuracy?
39:30 Diego: Yes, quantization can impact quality for certain tasks. We'll recommend quant profiles and run evals on your prompt sets as part of the benchmark to measure regressions.
41:05 Sofia: Will we get per-route cost breakdowns during the pilot?
41:30 Aisha: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns per route/model — we'll share screenshots in the deck.
43:00 Evan: Ok final question — can you support multi-region failover for production?
43:30 Diego: We support routing by region and automated fallback; cross-region replication for cache is more complex but supported in Dedicated designs.
44:55 Aisha: Great, recap: Redwood sends onboarding and security docs (Aisha), Diego sends benchmark plan (Diego), Rivermark shares sample payloads and infra contact (Priya/ Evan). Runbook draft is attached; please comment.
46:20 Lina: I'll open a shared doc and grant edit permissions to the Rivermark team, and schedule a 60min benchmark kickoff for 10/13.
47:10 Priya: 10/13 works for us for kickoff, bench week 10/20. We'll aim to get the infra tickets opened by 10/06.
48:00 Markus: Also can you provide the data retention defaults and deletion procedure — we need that for our audit.
48:40 Lina: Included in the security packet — retention policies and deletion flows with sample API calls.
50:05 Aisha: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and next steps in email, and Lina will share the runbook link after this call.
51:30 Sofia: Thanks all, good session.
51:45 Speaker 2 (Aisha): End of recording.
